one_sentence: This document argues that divine providence is structurally isomorphic to a PID control system, with proportional, integral, and derivative modes of correction.
executive_summary: This document establishes a structural isomorphism between control theory (specifically PID feedback control systems) and Christian theology of divine providence. The core claim is that God's governance of human agents follows the same mathematical structure as a closed-loop control system: a setpoint (God's purpose/telos), an error signal (sin/deviation), and a three-mode controller (proportional = conscience/consequences, integral = cumulative sanctification, derivative = prophetic warning). The mapping resolves the sovereignty-free will paradox by showing that a controller can drive output toward a setpoint without replacing the plant's own dynamics. Key evidence includes 13 independent correspondences, predictions such as the necessity of all three temporal modes for zero steady-state error, and falsification conditions. The conclusion is that the PID decomposition is not an engineering invention but a discovery of a universal structure for temporal governance.
short_summary: This document is a structural isomorphism record mapping control theory to divine providence. The core claim is that providence operates as a PID controller with proportional (conscience), integral (sanctification), and derivative (prophetic warning) modes. Key evidence includes 13 independent correspondences, predictions about the necessity of all three modes, and falsification conditions. This matters because it formalizes the sovereignty-free will paradox as a standard controlled-system feature and provides a mathematical framework for understanding divine governance.
